title: Honest vs invalid evaluation, interactively
description: Course activity for Exercise 3 Section 3: choose k and watch three synchronized observed-vs-predicted panels -- A (valid), B (resubstitution), C (invalid leakage) -- recompute for standardized KNN regression on the exact same 360-feature age recipe as Section 2.
instructions: Drag the slider, use the arrow keys, or type an exact value in the number box to change k. All three panels use the same standardized 360-feature recipe and Exercise 2's own locked training/test split; only which rows were fitted on and which rows are scored differs between them.
k1Note: At k = 1, panels B and C are exactly perfect (R² = 1): every evaluated point is its own nearest neighbour, at distance zero, so the prediction reproduces the observation by construction, not because anything was learned. Panel A at k = 1 is not perfect, because the test participants it evaluates were never used for fitting. k = 1 is therefore the clearest evidence that evaluating on fitted data is invalid -- not evidence that KNN generalises perfectly. Increasing k averages more observations and usually reduces this dramatic resubstitution effect.
reflectionPrompts: Set k = 1 and compare all three R² values. Which are exactly 1.000, and why exactly 1.000 rather than just "very high"?
Move k up toward its maximum. Do B and C stay close to A, move further away, or converge toward it? What does that tell you about how much k limits the optimism of B and C?
Panel C is invalid because the test rows were used for fitting. Name one thing about panel C's numbers that would look suspicious to someone who didn't know that -- and one thing that would not.
